text:
jamie: thanks everyone for coming to the all-hands — quick follow-up: a few folks asked for region/capacity clarity, especially APAC. will post the summary here and we can queue any Qs.

anita: thanks! is there an ETA on the additional APAC gpu pools we mentioned? a lot of customer requests coming in.

mike_infra: short answer: target is end of Q2 for the first incremental pool in ap-northeast-1, but that's supply-dependent. longer: we're doing staggered provisioning — small guaranteed pool first, then burstable capacity after validation.

devon: when you say "burstable" — does that go through the same autoscaler or a separate burst lane? curious about how fallbacks will work across regions.

mike_infra: good question. design: normal autoscaler (service level) scales within region for committed pools. burst lane is a cross-region overflow that can route to eu-west-1 or us-west-2 based on latency policy. routing uses our smart-routing weights + cost budget.

leo: will that overflow preserve customer data isolation requirements? some enterprise customers require no cross-region routing.

mike_infra: yes — routing honors customer pinning. if a workspace is configured with region: ap-northeast-1 and enforced data residency, we will not overflow it. burst lane only applies to non-pinned/opt-in workloads.

zuri: are there any changes to the canary rollout plan for models while the new pools are added? want to avoid double-canary situations.

mike_infra: we added a simple rule: if a model rollout is in canary on a region that is also receiving new capacity, the deployment controller will delay cross-region canaries until the pool health check passes. that reduces churn.

anita: sounds reasonable. any action items for product/solutions teams we should know about?

mike_infra: action items: (1) we will publish a short status page for APAC pool provisioning by tomorrow, (2) product to flag customers who are region-pinned so we can coordinate pre-provisioning, (3) devex to update the docs on routing/overflow behavior. tagging infra-bot to create tickets.

infra-bot: created tickets #INFRA-742 (APAC pool status page), #INFRA-743 (customer region pin audit), #DOCS-198 (routing behavior docs) :white_check_mark:

devon: awesome. a couple tiny asks: can we expose a read-only metric for "region headroom" in the console? would help account managers.

mike_infra: yes, plan to add a "headroom" gauge to the capacity dashboard. preliminary metric will show available GPU vCPU-equivalent and expected burstable capacity. ETA 2 weeks.

anita: one last thing — any recommended CLI to check current pool state?

mike_infra: use the admin CLI: `redwood infra pools status --region ap-northeast-1` will show pools, nodes, allocatable, and pending supply. sample output:```
NAME	STATUS	NODES	ALLOCATABLE
ap-n1-small	Ready	3	120 vGPU
ap-n1-burst	Pending	0	0
```

leo: thanks mike. will follow up with a short note to enterprise customers about pinning and overflow rules.

jamie: thanks team — appreciate the quick sync. if leadership needs to weigh in on prioritization, flag me or product. :thumbsup:

zuri: can we keep this thread as the single place for APAC capacity updates? helps avoid duplication.

mike_infra: yes — I'll post daily updates here until pools are fully provisioned. first status update tomorrow ~1100 PT.
